summary: Phase 149O.20L.6 -- Class-B Provisioning Authorization Record Capture. GOVERNANCE-ELECTION RECORD CAPTURE ONLY -- no production, contract, or real host change; no provisioning of any kind. Read Phase 149O.20L.5's and 149O.20L.5A's own planning documents directly and in full (not from any summary); found no material disagreement between them. Independently reconfirmed, read-only, that target/source state had not drifted since L.5A's own entry: same physical host, no dedicated deployment principal/clone/venv/Protected Root yet exist, HMIC-001 v1.3/HMRC-001 v1.1/HBDC-001 v1.0 and the three live Class-B verifier modules byte-unchanged since L.5A's own entry commit (fca87543). Reconstructed the live pcae decision-session/pcae governance-record CLI directly from its own --help output and source (never assumed from contract prose alone), and independently discovered the AESIC eligible-authority-citation mechanism (.pcae/authority-evaluation/templates/**, an existing, repository-managed, non-src/pcae/** data location, consumed at confirm time via the existing write_template/read_template convenience functions -- no new mechanism invented). Found that this repository had never published a real (non-test, non-fixture) CHGR before this phase -- every existing tests/fixtures/chgr/*.json artifact is explicitly synthetic; this phase's own published record is the first real Human Governance Record CHGR-001 has produced in this repository. Reconstructed the GPC6-REQ-075(b) precedent directly (first-person election, explicit non-extension list, closing confirmation sentence) and mirrored its properties through CHGR-001's own mechanism rather than hand-authoring a bespoke markdown file. Constructed the exact Boundary-P proposition from L.5A §19, restated its full explicit-exclusions list, and additionally presented a privileged-action disclosure (which of the nine planned actions require sudo/root vs. admin-controlled launch-config only) and a risk disclosure (new OS identity, ACL changes confined to new paths, partial-failure/rollback complexity, possible failure to reach COMPLIANT due to the unresolved packaging-metadata condition, possible continued HATP NOT READY even after Class-B COMPLIANT) to the human governance authority (Atila Madai) before requesting any election. The human governance authority responded with an explicit, first-person, verbatim APPROVE election, followed by a separately-requested explicit confirmation statement mirroring GPC6-REQ-075(b)'s own closing line -- neither fabricated, inferred, nor defaulted by this phase. Ran the full create -> evidence -> select -> preview -> confirm -> readiness -> publish CHGR-001 workflow exactly as reconstructed: session CDS-6476b6d1-e934-41b8-a57b-27426e18a4b5 (Created -> EvidenceReady -> DecisionSelected -> Confirmed, authority_evaluation_stage_1: indeterminate, disclosed and non-blocking per AESIC-001's own advisory-only design) -> readiness package prp-af987a7157804bdfb13dc06e6a060459 -> published CHGR chgr-d4343fa51b9743f3abaeb87a881a78b1. pcae governance-record inspect succeeded; pcae governance-record verify, supplied with all three related confirmation/provenance/integrity artifacts, returned outcome=verified with 7 of 8 checks passed (schema_shape, digest_self_consistency, lifecycle_structural_legality, confirmation_binding, assurance_truthfulness, provenance_consistency, integrity_consistency all passed; template_resolution honestly skipped -- this phase authored only the simpler AESIC citation document actually consumed by confirm, not a separate, optional, formal CHGR decision_template artifact, disclosed rather than fabricated). Verified the authorization artifact's binding to target, plan, source/commit, and contracts entirely through existing canonical CHGR fields (decision_subject, rationale, conditions, evidence declarations) -- no ad hoc field was added. Confirmed, via id/dscl/stat inspection and git status --short, that no real-host mutation of any kind occurred. This document's own companion test file (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_6_class_b_provisioning_authorization_record_capture.py, 18 tests, re-run three consecutive times, no flake) verifies: the published CHGR is a valid, published human_governance_record with selected_option_id=approve and decision_maker Atila Madai at assurance L0; rationale/conditions are non-empty and contain the required exclusion phrases; decision_subject cites both planning documents; the authored AESIC template names the human authority by name; pcae governance-record inspect/verify (via subprocess against the real installed pcae executable) both succeed with all non-skipped checks passing; this phase's own doc's Boundary-separation and phase-exit sections are explicit and not blurred; no real-provisioning/activation/certification token appears in this phase's own proposition/publication/exit-state sections; git diff --name-only HEAD contains no src/pcae/, docs/contracts/, or scripts/ entry; and no Protected Root or pcae OS principal exists on the real host after this phase. No real provisioning, certification, or activation was authorized or performed by this phase -- only an authorization record was captured. Recommends exactly one next phase: 149O.20L.7 -- Class-B Real Host Provisioning Execution, conditional on fresh re-verification of this CHGR's bindings at that phase's own entry.
